props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · runs on the game clock
props.title: One Angle, Two Numbers

B01.visual_intent: Act title 'One Angle, Two Numbers' (serif 40) top-left. A real Godot render in a framed window on the cream stage: a teal planet in the middle, a slate-blue moon circling it clockwise and a small amber meteor circling the moon, all on the warm grey stage color. No code is shown yet.
B01.motion_claim: The moon laps the planet and the meteor laps the moon, continuously, from the first frame.

show.event: window opens with the planet, moon and meteor already moving
still circling: the picture the whole film builds toward

B01.runner_up: manim drawing of a planet, moon and meteor on orbit rings
B01.why: A real render is the honest preview of the destination; a drawing would only claim it, and later acts rebuild exactly this picture.
B01.capture_spec: C01: Lab rect, lab-shaders/06-meteor-orbit.gdshader, square (480 x 480 logical canvas captured at 1920 x 1920), live TIME, 14 s, 30 fps, Forward+, no input. The moon laps the planet in 6.28 s, so about two laps show.

B02.visual_intent: A right triangle in grey outline on the cream stage, right angle at the lower right marked with a small square, the other angles at the lower left (30 degrees, marked by a thick terracotta arc and a small terracotta dot) and the top right. As each word is spoken the matching side thickens to ink and takes a 1 to 3 word serif label placed outside the outline: 'hypotenuse' on the long slanted side, 'opposite' on the right-hand vertical (across from the marked angle), 'adjacent' on the bottom (touching the marked angle). The 50 % frame holds the settled picture with the hypotenuse label and the marked angle.
B02.motion_claim: Each side thickens and takes its name exactly when the voice says it.

show.event: triangle draws; right-angle square
hypotenuse thickens, label lands
marked angle (arc and dot) appears at the lower left (done by 0.44)
opposite side thickens, label lands
adjacent side thickens, label lands

B02.why: Naming parts of a shape is pointing at them: each side lights up as its name is spoken, which a table cannot do.

B03.visual_intent: The same 30-degree triangle anchored at its marked lower-left corner. At the right, a readout in serif: 'opposite ÷ hypotenuse' over a large number. First the triangle scales (about 1.0, then 0.55, then 1.3) while thin grey ghosts of the earlier sizes stay nested at the same corner and the number stays 0.50 the whole time. After a hold (settled still at the 50 % frame: three nested outlines, '30°' and 0.50), the marked angle opens to 50 degrees: the hypotenuse swings up, the triangle reshapes, the angle label reads '50°' and the number settles at 0.77. A terracotta dot rides the top corner.
B03.motion_claim: The triangle grows and shrinks and the number does not move; the angle opens and the number does.

show.event: triangle at 30 degrees, readout 0.50
triangle scales down and up, ghosts nest, readout stays 0.50
settled: three nested outlines, 30°, 0.50 (hold through the midpoint)
angle opens to 50°, readout changes to 0.77

B03.why: Size changing while the number stays put is the claim, and only moving geometry with a live readout shows it.

B04.visual_intent: Left: the 30-degree triangle in grey, smaller. Right: three stacked outlined rows (padding, no fill behind text): 'sine · opposite ÷ hypotenuse', 'cosine · adjacent ÷ hypotenuse', 'tangent · opposite ÷ adjacent'. As each name is spoken its row lands and the two sides it uses thicken to ink on the triangle (sine: opposite and hypotenuse; cosine: adjacent and hypotenuse; tangent: opposite and adjacent) while the others return to grey. At the end 'SOH CAH TOA' sets under the rows with each first letter aligned to its row.
B04.motion_claim: Two sides of the triangle light up for each ratio as the voice names it.

show.event: triangle and the three empty rows
sine row lands; opposite and hypotenuse thicken
cosine row lands; adjacent and hypotenuse thicken
tangent row lands as text (done by 0.44; hold through the midpoint)
tangent's two sides thicken: opposite and adjacent
SOH CAH TOA sets under the rows

B04.why: The table would list the three ratios; lighting the matching sides on the triangle shows which sides each one uses.

B05.visual_intent: Two outlined boxes stacked on the cream stage, labelled 'sine' (upper) and 'cosine' (lower). At the left a small wedge token marked '30°' slides along a short drawn arrow into the sine box; a number token '0.50' slides out at the right. The same 30-degree token then enters the cosine box and '0.87' leaves it. One short line under the boxes: 'angle in, number out'. Arrows are drawn shapes, not glyphs; the 50 % frame holds with the sine result '0.50' settled.
B05.motion_claim: A 30-degree token enters each box and a number leaves it.

show.event: two boxes appear
30° token enters sine; 0.50 leaves
30° token enters cosine; 0.87 leaves
caption 'angle in, number out'

B05.why: Two tiny functions as boxes with a token passing through is the whole idea; isometric detail would add decoration, not meaning.
